messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: programming question
parts:
Hi,
I don't know that anyone can help me with this one, but I thought I
would ask. I have written my own 'fit' function for my personal class
('ExonEffectRmaPlm'). So I have the following functions (among others):
getFitFunction.ExonEffectRmaPlm (main changes)
getUnitFitFunction.ExonEffectRmaPlm
fit.ExonEffectRmaPlm
My getFitFunction calls some static functions, one of which gives a
temporary 'NA' value to something that is later updated and given a
permanent non-NA value. Most of the code is copied over from the
'RmaPlm' or 'ExonRmaPlm' functions.

My problem is this. When I run my 'fit' on all the units
('fit(units=NULL,force=T,...)') I get a NA value for one of the probes.
So that's an error in my function I need to figure out. But then if I
rerun my 'fit' on that unit only so I can debug it --
'fit(units=4920,force=T)' -- it doesn't return the NA anymore but a
numerical value. Is there anything anyone can think of as to why there
would be a difference? Or how I can debug this since I only see it when
it runs on all the units at once? Clearly I can't debug through 4000+
runs of the function. I've tried clearing out all the previous created
chip and probe files (and any cached results from them), so that it's
running truly from scratch and so I don't have to say units=NULL or
force=T, and it seems to be the same problem. I know it's impossible to
figure out the problems in a hypothetical function of someone else's,
but if there is anything in the behavior of how it uses force=T or
units=... , etc. that would help (because that's copied straight from
the standard code) I'd appreciate it.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] programming question
parts:
Hi,

Try to reproduce the problem with a minimal number of arrays. Replace
units=NULL with units=1:n where n == numberOfUnits(cdf). Do you still
get the problem? Then try with a smaller n, because I would surprise
me if you couldn't. Try to reproduce the problem with a minimum set
of units. When you have that it should be easier to track it down,
e.g. by adding details verbose output etc.

Moreover, fit() of ProbeLevelModel fits the model in chunks. When you
process all units you probably fit things in more than one chunk. So,
it could be that you get a side/memory effects from calling your
internal fit functions or similar more than ones. Try to reproduce
the problem with a minimal number of arrays. Then use units=NULL to
fit all and increase the 'ram' argument so you fit in only one chunk.
Do you still see the problem?

Just some thoughts.

/Henrik

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: programming question
parts:
Thanks, Henrik, for the suggestions. I discovered that actually when I
run my fit on all the arrays many different times (and completely
delete, everything so it is fresh) it is different units each time that
get the NAs -- i.e. not reproducibly the same units, which is probably
why it wasn't NA the next time I fit it and had nothing to do with force
or units arguments. Moreover, the NA originates in the output from the
call to the affyPLM function, not my function. Clearly this doesn't
happen with the standard fit function, so I have to track this down
somehow and figure out what I could have changed! But thanks for the
suggestions and it still might be something to do with the batches since
that is the only thing that could be changing between one call and the
next to give me different results each time.
Best,
Elizabeth
